review_type: single AI curator; full received final answer read; model identity visible

errors.quote: a dose that maximizes the proportion of cells in G1 arrest
errors.issue: This calibrates an arrest/viability phenotype, not matched DNA-damage load. No independent initial lesion assay across p53 states is specified. The same dose or maximal arrest does not establish equivalent delivered injury.

errors.quote: This allows acute, titratable depletion of endogenous p53 upon addition of the auxin analog
errors.issue: An AID-tagged protein plus IAA in mammalian cells also requires the appropriate introduced TIR1-containing degradation machinery. This essential engineered component is omitted; specify and validate the matched tag/receptor/ligand system.

errors.quote: To guarantee isolation of true G1 arrest from death and artifacts
errors.issue: Viability/Annexin gating cannot guarantee removal of survivor-selection bias. Keep a starting cohort, cumulative phase-specific death and detached-cell counts, and a joint S-entry/death analysis; excluding dying cells does not reverse altered composition.

errors.quote: a cessation of division events in individual lineages (true arrest)
errors.issue: No division is not G1-specific: cells may be in S or G2 arrest or slowly cycling. Include a validated live G1/S assignment, baseline phase eligibility and a duration calibrated to untreated G1 transit.

errors.quote: must show no statistically significant difference in baseline cell-cycle distribution
errors.issue: A nonsignificant test does not establish equivalence or rule out a biologically important baseline effect. Conversely a genuine baseline p53 effect does not uniquely show reagent toxicity. Use justified equivalence margins and a baseline-adjusted damage interaction.

errors.quote: The strictly standardized mean difference (or ANOVA interaction term)
errors.issue: Specify a single exact contrast incorporating mock baselines, a primary timepoint, culture-level variance/power plan, meaningful loss/restoration margins and uncertainty. The three damaged-state comparison and unspecified statistical restoration rule do not supply these.

errors.quote: 80–120% restoration of WT p53 levels in the Dox-rescued condition relative to baseline
errors.issue: Matching basal protein alone is insufficient when damage induces p53. Verify the rescued post-damage abundance, dynamics and functional output against the intact parental response, with matched pretreatment duration.

rationale: Recognizes the motivation for isogenic acute loss, rescue and death measurement, but the proposed protocol does not actually verify matched injury, lacks essential AID machinery and live G1/S identification, and overclaims what survivor gating and nonsignificant baseline tests establish. Primary contrast, power and rescue kinetics are materially underspecified.
reference_guardrails: The complete final answers from DeepSeek and Gemini, the exact packet and full reference/curator clarification were personally read. No API judge, hidden reasoning or real experiment was used.

The reference body retains survivor-only and damage-recalibration language. Its explicit clarification takes precedence: use starting-cohort denominators and competing death outcomes; match initial delivered injury without removing later repair differences caused by p53.

A partial loss of arrest supports contribution to the response. Full necessity for the defined response requires evidence that meaningful damage-induced arrest is absent after effective loss, with uncertainty and rescue specificity. Do not demand exact zero or universal dependence.

Common external exposure and state-specific lesion matching estimate different effects. Neither is rejected categorically if justified and reported. Merely adjusting for a post-treatment mediator is not automatically a matched-damage causal experiment.

Near-endogenous rescue includes damage-induced kinetics and cell-to-cell abundance; successful damage-dependent rescue does not prove p53-alone sufficiency. Assay/dose calibration proposals are legitimate because identities and timings were not supplied.

Predetermined outcome-based rejection can still select confirmatory results. Distinguish technical failure from biological death, lesion burden or negative arrest outcomes and preserve the latter in reporting.

Live tracking must distinguish S entry followed by death, no S entry before death, persistent viable G1, and unresolved tracking. No informative-loss mechanism is cured by labeling all loss censoring.

The source audit here is limited to indexed primary-paper abstract/metadata excerpts; PubMed/PMC full-page access was challenged. No full historical methods audit is claimed. Scoring follows the supplied hypothetical packet rather than unavailable methods.

AID-mediated depletion recognizes a protein tag: synonymous recoding does not make an otherwise identical tagged protein resistant. Untagged rescue is a valid alternative. The AID2 paper abstract, introduction and initial results through the reporter comparisons were read, not its full supplementary protocol.

Both answers are within the 3500-word limit. DeepSeek receives credit for explicitly defining a starting-G1 denominator and a damage-by-rescue interaction; it is not treated as solely a survivor-only design.

A short endpoint nucleotide pulse is not cumulative S-entry history. No division alone does not identify G1 arrest. Appropriate live phase assignment and event history resolve these distinct problems.
